fences.text: (CHAR-03 再利用) A Japanese woman in her mid 40s walks away from the camera along a narrow mountain trail in a forest near Setana, southwestern Hokkaido, in early April early spring: bare deciduous trees, brown leaf litter, fresh green shoots of wild garlic on the slope, No snow anywhere, no frost, no ice, no winter. She wears a MAROON field jacket (deep red-brown, NOT green, NOT grey, NOT olive), charcoal trousers, dark hair tied low at the nape in a short low bun, NOT a ponytail, and carries a small plain canvas bag over one shoulder. Seen from directly behind, mid-stride with one foot lifted, only her back visible, no face visible. Unseen by her, far behind her on the trail at the edge of the bamboo thicket, an adult male Hokkaido brown bear about 2 metres long and roughly 150 to 250 kilograms has stepped out ON ALL FOURS, NOT upright, head dropped low, ears pinned flat, the fur along its neck bristled up into a raised ridge, fixed on her back. Framed from adult eye height about five metres behind her, the trail leading into the middle of the frame. Soft overcast daylight, quiet uneasy mood, muted natural tones. Photorealistic, shot on RED camera. Documentary style. 16:9 aspect ratio. Generate 1 image.
